incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prod-rt cluster prod-rt-1 — kv-prefix cache size spiked 18x in 5m, sustained increased tail latency. Error rate > 3% on /v1/generate. Pager: maya

maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing 200ms -> 1.2s p95 on chat-gen and OOM alerts on a couple nodes.

juan (eng-runtime): grabbing logs. initial suspicion: prefix hashing churn — looks like repeated near-duplicates generating distinct cache keys, causing cache blowup + slower continuous batching.

sarah (eng-sre): memory alarms triggered on gpu-hosts-5/7/8. Eviction not kicking in quickly enough. Can we throttle batching while we investigate?

maya (oncall): yes. temporarily reducing batch window and max tokens. issuing change now.

maya (oncall): (runbook) apply quick config:
```
# reduce batching to prioritize latency
service.config.batch_max_tokens=1024
service.config.batch_max_items=12
service.config.batch_latency_ms=20
```

maya (oncall): deployed to prod-rt-1 via rollout job rjob/4872 (canary 10%). monitoring.

alex (support): Support checking customer impact. Early hit: 3 high-traffic customers (acme-ai, fastdocs, chatflow) reporting 5xx and timeouts. Logged CS tickets.

li (eng-ml): looking at prefix hashing code — there was a recent tokenizer tweak in PR #3221 that changed normalization for templated prompts. That can cause same logical prompt to map to different token sequences -> different prefix keys. Noticed increased entropy in hash outputs in the last deploy.

juan (eng-runtime): confirming — correlation between deploy timestamp and start of cache growth. Hash keys show same semantic prefix but different token-level ids.

juan (eng-runtime): quick mitigation idea: force eviction for suspicious prefix pattern (templated prompts) and patch hashing to be backward-compatible. Also consider short-term disabling prefix caching for chat endpoints.

sarah (eng-sre): eviction command ready, testing on staging then will run on prod-rt-1.

sarah (eng-sre): exec: `POST /admin/cache/evict` payload: `{"match_prefix":"prompt_tpl_v2:", "force": true}`

juan (eng-runtime): running eviction on the three hottest hosts now.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: eviction job started by sarah at 1781234602 — job-id evict-1781-9

maya (oncall): after eviction, mem usage dropping on hosts 5/7/8. latency p95 down to ~310ms. Error rate falling but still above baseline.

li (eng-ml): prepping PR to restore consistent tokenization behavior and add explicit hash salt/versioning so we can rotate safely. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3299 (patch + regression test).

juan (eng-runtime): propose: rollback tokenizer change from PR #3221 on prod-rt-1 as a hotfix, then deploy li's forward-compatible hashing in next patch. Rollback decreases risk of repeated cache churn. Thoughts?

emily (product): prioritize stability — go ahead with rollback if safe. Need short customer-facing note once stabilized.

alex (support): will prepare status update for affected customers: mention mitigation in progress, reduced perf while we finish hotfix, ETA 2h.

maya (oncall): starting rollback of tokenizer change on canary nodes now (rjob/4873 rollback). Monitoring canary.

incident-bot: DEPLOY_EVENT: rollback canary started by maya at 1781234625 — watching for errors.

juan (eng-runtime): canary looks good for 3 minutes, no regressions in other signals. starting ramp to 30%.

maya (oncall): ramping to 30%. p95 continues to improve.

sarah (eng-sre): memory alarms cleared on 5/7/8. error rate back to ~0.4% (acceptable).

li (eng-ml): PR #3299 is ready for merge (includes deterministic hash with version tag and tokenizer normalization tests). Will cut a release once we confirm rollback fully stable.

maya (oncall): handing off — I need to jump to another pager. Juan will own the incident from here.

juan (eng-runtime): taking over. Summary: root cause = tokenizer change created token-level divergence -> prefix hash churn -> cache blowup -> continuous batching backpressure -> perf cliff. Mitigations done: reduced batching params, forced eviction, rollback tokenizer change canary -> ramp -> successful. Next steps: merge forward-compatible hash in PR #3299, add automated detection for abrupt cache key entropy shifts, and add safe-guard to disable prefix cache when eviction rate > threshold.

juan (eng-runtime): customers impacted: acme-ai (ticket #4321), fastdocs (#4322), chatflow (#4323). alex will send status email.

alex (support): prepping update now. ETA 15m for first customer note.

emily (product): will draft customer postmortem blurb for tomorrow: root cause, actions taken, timeline, corrective plan.

maya (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes in incident tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026 — tagging eng-runtime+eng-ml+eng-sre.

juan (eng-runtime): logging all commands and chat here for handoff. followups assigned:
- li: finish merge + rolling release (PR #3299)
- juan: implement cache auto-disable threshold (incident mitigation)
- sarah: add alert for hash entropy spike and eviction rate high
- alex: customer comms and impact log

sarah (eng-sre): scheduling postmortem meeting for 24h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT_STATUS: resolved-> mitigated at 1781234689 — monitoring for 2h.

juan (eng-runtime): I'll keep monitoring. ping me if anything new shows up. :thumbsup:
